explanation: Makers soak strips of inner bark, usually from the paper mulberry tree, then beat them thin and wide with wooden mallets before painting or stamping designs.

claims.text: Tapa is a cloth made from beaten tree bark in Pacific islands including Tonga and Samoa.
Tapa is not made from woven palm leaves, felted goat hair or pressed seaweed.
Tapa makers soak the inner bark, usually of the paper mulberry tree, and beat it thin with wooden mallets.
Tapa is decorated by painting or by rubbing or stamping designs onto it.
